name: Plymouth Gin Original Strength
base_ingredient: Grain alcohol with soft Dartmoor water
production: Botanicals macerated in grain alcohol and Dartmoor water
Batch-distilled in a single Victorian copper pot still (1855)
history: 1431 | Black Friars building (former Dominican monastery) built (Absolut Group page says 1400s)
1793 | Gin production begins; Plymouth Gin founded by Fox & Williamson
1850 | Royal Navy buys over 1,000 barrels of Plymouth Gin a year
1930 | The Savoy Cocktail Book lists Plymouth Gin in 23 recipes
2008 | Pernod Ricard acquires V&S and Plymouth Gin
palate: Smooth, deep, earthy yet fresh and lemony
serve_official: Dry Martini, Gimlet, or G&T with a lemon twist (retailer)
notes: Owner page (The Absolut Group) used for history and botanicals.
